name: Geoffrey Hinton
title: The Godfather of AI says we cannot afford to get it wrong
speaker: Geoffrey Hinton
horizon: Within approximately 30 years, in the interviewer’s question that Hinton answers
conditions: Subjective estimate; explicitly uncertain and revisable, not a measured probability
summary: Hinton endorses 10–20% as reasonable while emphasizing profound uncertainty. A later August 2026 interview gives no replacement percentage.
quote: 10% to 20% seemed like reasonable numbers to me

laterContext.summary: Host repeats the old range. Hinton emphasizes that it is an intuitive guess, says caring-AI ideas have made him somewhat less scared, and does not state a new percentage.

name: Gary Marcus
title: Why my p(doom) has risen, dramatically
speaker: Gary Marcus
definition: AI-related catastrophic danger discussed through misuse, reckless deployment and concentrated power; no exact extinction-only endpoint
conditions: Dated update after Grok-related concerns; hypothetical worst circumstances, not certainty
summary: Marcus raises his personal estimate to about 3%, emphasizing reckless powerful actors rather than assuming present LLMs become autonomous superintelligence.
comparisonClass: broad catastrophe definition; approximate comparison only

name: Dario Amodei
title: Amodei on AI: 25% chance things go badly
speaker: Dario Amodei

name: Max Tegmark
title: Max Tegmark vs. Dean Ball: Should We BAN Superintelligence?
speaker: Max Tegmark
definition: Loss of human control after superintelligence deployment
conditions: Explicitly conditional on continuing without predeployment safety regulation; not an unconditional prediction that regulation will fail to materialize
summary: At 01:17:05 Tegmark estimates greater than 90% loss of control under continued unregulated deployment. At 01:27:58 he reiterates the condition and expresses optimism about regulation.
quote: When I said P(doom) of over 90%, that was if we do no regulation.
comparisonClass: conditional scenario; do not score against unconditional simulated percentage

name: Noah Smith
title: Here’s how we’re all going to die
speaker: Noah Smith
definition: AI-enabled bioterrorism; civilization collapse and severe destruction are distinct endpoints, not necessarily human extinction or permanent disempowerment
horizon: No numerical forecast horizon; the essay’s illustrative scenario starts in 2029
conditions: AI-enabled bioterrorism specifically; informal estimates rather than exhaustive all-cause AI risk
summary: Smith estimates a 10% collapse risk and 30% severe destruction risk from AI-enabled bioterrorism. These must remain separate from an extinction-only P(doom).
quote: about a 10% chance of bringing down civilization
comparisonClass: different outcome definition; do not report numerical calibration error

name: Noah Smith
title: This Top Economist’s P(Doom) Just Shot Up 10x! Noah Smith Returns To Explain His Update
speaker: Noah Smith
percentageOrRange: roughly 10% collapse; does not endorse host’s 5% permanent doom
definition: Civilization collapse with survivors; distinguishes this from total extinction and permanent inability to recover
conditions: Powerful agents misused by humans, especially bioterror; distinguishes these from long-term machine-god scenarios
summary: The speaker-labeled exchange separates recoverable collapse from permanent doom. Do not convert the host’s suggested 5% into Smith’s estimate or treat the episode title as sufficient evidence.
comparisonClass: clarifying evidence, not a second independent benchmark
